title: Association of Annual mRNA COVID-19 Booster Vaccination With Changes in Allostatic Load in the Post-Pandemic Era: A Longitudinal Primary Care Cohort Study
summary:
Background: Long-lasting strain wears the body down. This wear can be measured with several simple values from blood and circulation and combined into a single figure. A high figure goes together with more illness and faster ageing.
Question: We want to know whether the yearly booster vaccination against the coronavirus affects how quickly this bodily wear increases in the years after the pandemic.
Approach: We analyse data from a large family doctor's practice in the Black Forest that has carefully recorded all examinations, laboratory values and vaccinations for many years. We compare people by how often they received a booster: every year, occasionally, or not at all. We then observe how their figure changes over time, especially from the year 2022 onward. The study does not change anyone's treatment; we use existing data and, from 2026, add a few simple tests of physical fitness. In this way we hope to better understand the benefits and risks of repeated booster vaccination for long-term health.
conditions: Cumulative physiological burden (allostatic load) and its change in the context of repeated mRNA COVID-19 booster vaccinations in the post-pandemic period. Not a single disease entity: the study examines the trajectory of an integrative biomarker score (Allostatic Load Index) in an adult primary care population, complemented by respiratory morbidity (COPD exacerbations, acute respiratory infections) as clinical correlates.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
In addition to the minimum age (≥ 18 years on the index date 01 Jan 2020): (1) at least 3 years of continuous practice enrolment in the pre-pandemic period 2015–2019; (2) at least 2 ALI-relevant laboratory measurements in the pre-pandemic period (2015–2019) and at least 2 from 01 Jan 2022 until data extraction; (3) documented COVID-19 vaccination history ('no vaccination' is a valid status). Part B (prospective): additionally, continued care at the practice during 2026.
Exclusion criteria:
(1) Terminally ill individuals with a life expectancy below 6 months at study start (physician's assessment); (2) individuals without any laboratory documentation during the study period; (3) individuals who died or moved away from the catchment area before 01 Jan 2022.
